record.title: Fixed-SAE Track traces bounded, format-heavy RL shifts in a small reasoning model
record.summary: A September 14, 2026 arXiv paper introduces Fixed-SAE Track: it trains one shared sparse autoencoder per analyzed layer on activations pooled across a base model and its RL checkpoints, then freezes the feature directions to track representation shifts. In the main Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct math-RL setting, the authors report gradual late-layer drift concentrated in formatting and reasoning scaffolds. Steering amplified features at dose α=10 raises strict accuracy from 0.050 to 0.192, close to the short-RL final model’s 0.175, while lenient reasoning accuracy changes more modestly. The paper also reports that all 29 selected GSM8K problems that shift from greedy-base-wrong to RL-right are solved by base sampling at k=64; however, 2000 additional RL steps raise lenient accuracy from 0.300 to 0.408, and directly injecting a necessary reasoning feature set recovers little. The approximately 80% headline therefore concerns a bounded short-RL extractability/format effect, not a general claim that RL only elicits existing capability. Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
organizations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce Fixed-SAE Track, which trains one shared SAE per analyzed layer on pooled activations from a base model and RL checkpoints, then re-encodes all checkpoints through the frozen dictionary to track feature shifts using fixed directions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the main Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct mathematical RL setting, the authors report small, gradual, late-layer feature drift concentrated in formatting scaffolds and ladder tokens. At steering dose α=10, steering amplified features raises strict accuracy from 0.050 to 0.192 versus 0.175 for the short-RL final model, while lenient accuracy changes more modestly.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For 29 GSM8K problems that are wrong under greedy base decoding but correct after RL, the authors report base pass@k rises to 1.00 at k=64; they also report that continuing training for 2000 steps raises lenient accuracy from 0.300 to 0.408. These results qualify the claim that short RL mainly elicits existing sampled capability: sustained training can add reasoning performance in this regime.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that RL generally only elicits pre-existing capabilities or that the headline steering recovery is a general fraction of RL’s gain; the ~80% framing concerns a short-training strict-accuracy/extractability effect, while directly injecting a reasoning feature set recovers little.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of Fixed-SAE Track, feature interpretations or steering results has been inspected.
The main mechanistic claims center on one small model family, mathematical RL and a specific fixed SAE layer; broader model, task and algorithm transfer remains uncertain.

The approximately 80% steering recovery framing refers to the short-RL strict-accuracy/extractability effect; sustained training also improves lenient accuracy, and static injection of the reasoning feature set recovers little.
The base pass@64 result covers the 29 selected GSM8K problems that switch from greedy-base-wrong to RL-right; it does not establish broad capability presence across harder tasks or sampling budgets.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, a shared SAE dictionary across RL checkpoints offers a useful method for separating representation drift from feature-index mismatch, and the reported interventions suggest short-run math-RL gains can partly reflect improved answer-format extractability. This could change how post-training gains are mechanistically interpreted, but the main evidence is one small model/task regime, author-run and explicitly qualified by modest sustained-training reasoning gains.
limitations: All evidence is from the author-reported arXiv v1 paper; no independent reproduction was performed.
The main representational analysis focuses on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct mathematical RL and a fixed SAE at layer 27, with some layer comparisons; broader transfer is unknown.

The approximately 80% headline describes steering recovery of a short-RL strict-accuracy/extractability effect; lenient reasoning accuracy changes more modestly, and sustained training raises it further.
Among 29 GSM8K problems wrong under greedy base decoding but right after RL, base sampling solves all by k=64; this selected set does not establish general capability boundaries.
A reasoning feature set is reported as causally necessary under ablation, but direct static injection recovers only a small fraction of the RL gain.

brief.summary: A September 14, 2026 arXiv paper introduces Fixed-SAE Track: it trains one shared sparse autoencoder per analyzed layer on activations pooled across a base model and its RL checkpoints, then freezes the feature directions to track representation shifts. technical.claimed_result: The authors report small gradual late-layer drift, mostly in formatting/scaffolding features, and that steering amplified features in the base model reproduces much of short-RL strict-accuracy/tag-rate gains. They report base pass@64 solves all 29 selected RL-fixed GSM8K problems and sustained training adds lenient accuracy; the paper therefore qualifies the short-RL elicitation result.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public v1 paper defines a pooled shared-SAE tracking method and reports activation analyses and steering/ablation experiments. These establish what the authors measured and claim, not independent confirmation of the mechanistic interpretation.
technical.mechanism: Pool activation vectors across base and RL checkpoints, train and freeze a shared TopK SAE per layer, and compare stable latent activations across checkpoints. Use token attribution and causal steering/ablation to distinguish feature correlations from tested sufficiency/necessity.
technical.regime: Primarily Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct math RL, GRPO and layer-27 SAE analysis, with strict-format and lenient-reasoning metrics; 29 selected GSM8K problems for base pass@64; a 2000-step continuation for sustained training.
technical.reproducibility: The full arXiv paper and appendices are public and report controls and cross-run/cross-algorithm analyses, but no independent implementation or reproduction was inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: For steering sufficiency, the short-RL final checkpoint is compared with the base model under amplified-feature and random-direction interventions. For base capability, the comparator is greedy decoding versus sampling pass@k on the selected 29 GSM8K items. These comparisons answer different questions and should not be collapsed into one general RL effect.

brief.title: Fixed-SAE Track traces bounded, format-heavy RL shifts in a small reasoning model
brief.why_it_matters: A shared fixed feature basis can make checkpoint-to-checkpoint interpretability less dependent on matching separately trained SAE features. The reported interventions suggest some short-run mathematical RL gains may reflect answer-format extractability, while the paper also finds genuine reasoning gains under sustained training. This distinction could change how post-training gains are measured and interpreted, but the evidence remains author-reported and narrow in model/task regime.
